$comment: The words an amount is written or said with, in Urdu script, Roman Urdu and English, for the amount grammar (docs/roadmap/amount-parser.md): mm_core's parseAmount and formatAmountWords, and later its findAmounts and the TypeScript ports. Written by hand and NOT YET REVIEWED by a native speaker (reviewed: false; the review is work item 2, through docs/roadmap/urdu-review.md; review.check_first lists what to look at first). In every list the first spelling is the one to write; the others are only read. A spelling, after normalise, belongs to one entry only: a number, a fraction, a multiplier, a currency marker, a foreign currency, a filler or a connector. ambiguous lists tokens with a second everyday meaning: 'free_text' tokens are read in a single amount field and make an amount in free text ambiguous; 'spaced' tokens are also read in free text when joined to digits; 'always' tokens are never read and make any amount they touch ambiguous, because ignoring them would misread it. homographs lists other meanings the grammar's other rules already keep apart, for the review. A multiplier's plural forms are read only after a number ('5 lakhs'); on their own ('lakhs of rupees') they are vague and ambiguous. not_included lists spellings left out on purpose. Every addition needs a vector in contracts/amount_vectors.json.

normalise.$comment: Applied to the text, and to every spelling here, before matching. It extends the plan's normalisation (digits, direction marks, lower case) with the Arabic keyboard's letters and with marks that never tell two number words apart. Each fold is one code point for one or two, so a span can be mapped back to the original text.
normalise.digits: As normalizeDigits (packages/mm_core/lib/src/text/digits.dart): Arabic-Indic, Extended Arabic-Indic (Urdu) and full-width digits become ASCII.

fractions.note: One and a half, on its own or before a multiplier: ڈیڑھ لاکھ 150,000; derh sau 150. Takes no number after it. dedh is the roadmap's spelling.
Two and a half, on its own or before a multiplier: dhai lakh 250,000. Takes no number after it.

A quarter less than the number after it: paune do lakh 175,000. alone: before a multiplier with no number it takes one (paune sau 75). tl-ur-fractional gives 'paune aaTh' as 7 1/2, an error: a quarter less than eight is 7 3/4, as tl-hi-fractional gives.
A half more than the number after it: sarhe teen hazar 3,500. From three upwards; 1 1/2 and 2 1/2 are derh and dhai. Never alone. Roman sare, saray and saare (also 'all') are refused; see ambiguous.
A quarter more than the number after it: sawa do lakh 225,000. alone: before a multiplier with no number it takes one (sawa lakh 125,000; sawa sau 125). سوا is also 'except' after کے; see ambiguous.

multipliers.note: ھزار: tl-ur-cardinal. hajar is how hazar is written where z is said as j, and is also a name; k is read joined to digits ('50k'); see ambiguous.
lakh and lac: cldr-en, parseMoneyInput. CLDR's short form L is refused; see ambiguous.
Owner question 1, as recommended: million and mn everywhere; a bare m only in a single amount field; see ambiguous. ملین is the English word as Urdu newspapers write it (general knowledge).
cr: cldr-en, parseMoneyInput; refused in free text, where bank messages use Cr for 'credit'; see ambiguous.
Short-scale billion (10^9), as Pakistani English uses it. بلین is the Urdu word as Urdu newspapers write it (general knowledge). Roman arab is also 'Arab'; see ambiguous.
cldr-ur-rbnf and cldr-ur use کھرب for 10^11. Roman kharab is also 'bad' (خراب) and is refused; see ambiguous. English has no single word.

currency.note: Every marker parseMoneyInput reads is here (Rs, Rs., PKR, ₨, rupee, rupees, روپے, روپیہ, روپیے, a trailing /-). cldr-ur gives پاکستانی روپیہ and the symbol Rs; cldr-en gives PKR.

foreign_currency.note: Owners abroad (decision 1) may write amounts in the currency they earn. An amount next to one of these is not in rupees and is never read as rupees. ₹ is the Indian rupee. sar (Saudi riyal) is also Roman 'head' (سر); a refusal there only asks the person to confirm.

fillers.note: 'only', as on cheques and receipts ('Rupees fifty thousand only', 'پچاس ہزار روپے صرف'). Never changes the amount.

connectors.note: British English joins the last group with 'and' ('one hundred and fifty'). Read only in English and only in a single amount field; see ambiguous. Roman aur and Urdu اور are refused.

ambiguous.why: joins groups ('one hundred and fifty'), or joins two amounts in a sentence ('1 lakh and 50 is pending').
a misspelt assi (eighty), or aisi (such), or Punjabi 'we'.
'and' or 'more': 'do lakh aur pachas hazar' is 250,000, or 200,000 and 50,000 more.
short form of billion (cldr-en), or a letter.
crore, or 'credit' on bank statements and messages ('Rs 5,000.00 Cr').
a misspelt dhai, or 'midwife' (دائی): 'dai lakh' may mean 250,000.
a misspelt derh, or 'late' (دیر): 'der lakh' may mean 150,000.
two, or the verb 'give' after another verb: 'bhej do hazar rupay' can mean 1,000 or 2,000. Only two after a fraction word ('sawa do') or a currency marker, which findAmounts (work item 5) may use.
thousand, or the given name Hajar.
a fraction the grammar does not read; ignoring it would misread the amount beside it.
thousand, or the Roman chat spelling of ke and ki ('us k pas'). Read joined to digits ('50k') anywhere; spaced ('50 k') only in a single amount field.
Indian English short form of lakh (cldr-en), or litre.
million, or minutes, metres, or Roman main (I) and mein (in). Owner question 1: read only in a single amount field.
short form of million, or Roman mil (found, received): '50 hazar mil gaye'.
English 'or' ('50 or 60 thousand'), or the Roman spelling of aur (and).
a paisa (a hundredth of a rupee), or 'money'. Paisa words are not in the grammar: '50 paise' is half a rupee, not 50 rupees.
a quarter (پاؤ), used for weight; not in the grammar.
three quarters (پون), or a misspelt paon (foot).
three quarters (پونا); not in the grammar.
a decimal point said in words: ignoring it would read 'do point paanch lakh' (2.5 lakh) as 5 lakh.
a fraction the grammar does not read.
'all' (سارے), or a misspelt sarhe: 'sare do lakh' is 200,000 or 250,000.
seventy, or the given name Sattar.
seventy, or the given name Sattar: 'Sattar hazar rupay de gaya'.
hundred, or English 'so', or Roman so (sleep).
eighty, or 'that very': 'اسی ہزار روپے میں سے' is 'out of that same 1,000' or 'out of 80,000'.
nineteen, or the given name Anees: 'انیس ہزار روپے دے گیا'.
two, or the verb 'give' after another verb: 'بھیج دو ہزار روپے' can mean 1,000 or 2,000. Only two after a fraction word ('سوا دو') or a currency marker, as do.
a quarter more, or 'except' after کے or a possessive: 'اس کے سوا دو لاکھ' is 'apart from this, 2 lakh' or '2.25 lakh'.
a quarter, used for weight; not in the grammar.
a decimal point said in words, as point.
three quarters; not in the grammar.
three quarters; not in the grammar.
'hundreds of billions of', a vague amount.

homographs.why: also the article 'a'; before a multiplier both readings are one.
also hyperbole ('lakh koshish'); findAmounts should not read a bare multiplier without a currency marker or a number beside it.
also the verb 'sleep' ('سو گیا') and a literary 'so'.
also 'new' in phrases such as 'سالِ نو'.
also a Persian word for 'why', rare in everyday Urdu.

a chat short form of hazar; no source seen.
Punjabi and some Urdu chat spelling of ek; add with a vector if the pilot shows it.
a Roman spelling of کھرب; no source seen.
the singular short form of rupee ('Re. 1'); also an interjection.
hedges such as taqreeban, lagbhag, about, around: the amount is read and the read-back shows it; findAmounts (work item 5) decides whether to flag them.
a Roman spelling of teen (three), also English 'tin'.
'all'; a misspelt ساڑھے is rarer in Urdu script than sare in Roman Urdu, and 'سارے دو لاکھ' read as 200,000 is right for 'all two lakh'.
